Updates depend on eachother often. However, Windows Update sometimes messes up the order in which updates have to be installed. Depths of winter. Realised I'd run out of my medication when I went to take it at night. Repeat script had ended, so I didn't actually have the paper to get a new supply. Went a long way across the city to try out-of-hours GP - no luck. Rang up my own GP for an emergency appointment for the next day - the only one available was at 6pm. I accepted it. By this point I was already starting to shake, and I felt very, very, irrationally uneasy. I also felt quite queasy, though I managed to keep some food down. I decided to take an early bed, extra sleepers, and see how the next day went.

I barely slept a wink. I yawned constantly and felt very groggy, but I could not for the life of me sleep. I ended up getting up at 5 and taking a taxi (which I really couldn't financially excuse) to the out-of-hours GP for another try. In the taxi, my eyes rolled back into my head and I could have sworn I was going to have a fit. Everything scared me. I remember passing a few pigeons in the street and having this nebulous idea that they were rabid or some such. The out-of-hours GP staff told me that, because my medication is controlled, I couldn't get it there. I'd even brought my passport and a copy of an old paper script. I get the feeling that health professionals don't really like medicines!

I took a bus home, which was probably a bad move, as I got a lot of strange looks, with my paranoid eyes and my jerking and twitching. If I sat down for too long, I couldn't stand up properly. As the long bus journey wore on, I started to, I think, hallucinate. I saw the silhouettes of figures seeping out of the walls of the bus, and the floor of the bus moved like deep mud. When I eventually got off, I was shaking all over, and barely needed to lie down on my bed - I just fell onto it! I slept for a long time, from about 7am to 3pm, out of sheer exhaustion. I had terrible dreams.

6pm finally rolled around, but the doc didn't take me until around the time the surgery was beginning to close. I think I was the very last patient! By the time I had my renewed slip, my usual pharmacy had closed. I searched on my phone for pharmacies that open late, rand found one not too far away. I still didn't want to risk walking, so I got yet another taxi. I was thanking God for social healthcare.

I arrived at the all-night pharmacy. There was a long queue outside. I was a bit apprehensive at first, and thought about finding a different place, but I had to save money and I had to get my medicine quickly. When I eventually got in, to the credit of the pharmacist and technicians, they were very quick to make up my script. However, in front of a shop crowded with a mix of probable recreational users and little old ladies, the girl at the till called out: "[my name], here's your [controlled med]!". I think I was lucky to get out of there alive.

tl;dr my minor inconvenience: running out of medicine
